headline: Seasonal Forest Road and Historic Site Access
reservation: Most campgrounds and historic sites like the Medicine Wheel are seasonal and require official status checks. While general forest access is open, specific developed sites and group areas may require booking via the national reservation system; always verify current fire restrictions.

days.title: Alpine Heights and Ancient Landmarks

stops.name: Steamboat Point
stops.detail: Ascend this prominent limestone outcrop for panoramic views across the Bighorn Basin.

stops.name: Medicine Wheel National Historic Landmark
stops.detail: Walk the high-altitude path to this sacred stone structure, used for centuries by indigenous tribes.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours for steep mountain grades; conditions vary.
days.note: Medicine Wheel is at nearly 10,000 feet; snow may block access through late June.

days.title: Canyon Falls and Glacial Lakes

stops.name: Shell Falls
stops.detail: Observe the powerful drop where water cuts through ancient granite at this interpretive site.

stops.name: Sibley Lake
stops.detail: Enjoy the quiet alpine waters for shore fishing or a stroll through the pine forest.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; conditions vary with mountain weather.
days.note: Shell Falls Interpretive Center has limited seasonal hours; check before arrival.

days.title: Cloud Peak Skyway and High Passes

stops.name: Powder River Pass
stops.detail: Stand at the highest point on Highway 16, reaching 9,666 feet with views of the Cloud Peak Wilderness.

stops.name: Tensleep Canyon
stops.detail: Drive through the dramatic limestone switchbacks and observe the popular rock climbing walls.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours; conditions vary based on vehicle braking needs.
days.note: Use low gears on the descent into Ten Sleep to avoid brake overheating.

intel.title: Trailhead Demand
intel.text: West Tensleep Trailhead often reaches capacity during July weekends due to wilderness access. Arrive before mid-morning to secure a spot for day hikes.

intel.title: High Country Dead Zones
intel.text: Expect total loss of signal on Highway 14 and Highway 16 between gateway cities. Satellite messengers are recommended for backcountry travelers.

intel.title: Last Chance Supplies
intel.text: Fuel is generally unavailable between Sheridan/Buffalo and the mountain interior. Top off tanks before beginning the ascent.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Openings
intel.text: High-altitude forest roads typically open in mid-June and close by late October. Check the Forest Service road status map for current gate openings.

intel.title: Steep Grade Navigation
intel.text: Highway 14 contains 10% grades and sharp switchbacks. Drivers of large RVs should consult specific road grade maps before choosing their route.

plan.arrival: Land at Sheridan County Airport (SHR), gather mountain-specific supplies in Sheridan, and begin the ascent via Highway 14.
plan.vehicle: Reliable brakes are essential for mountain passes; check rental terms for operation on steep, winding grades.
plan.goldenHour: Steamboat Point offers views of the Bighorn Basin during the fading light; expect rapidly dropping temperatures after sunset.
